prompt:
Oracle 19c. This query from our Python service (python-oracledb) does a full table scan even though order_date is indexed. orders has 50M rows, order_date is DATE, index IDX_ORDERS_DATE (order_date). Stats were gathered last night.

cur.execute("""
    SELECT id, customer_id, total
    FROM orders
    WHERE order_date >= :start_ts AND order_date < :end_ts
""", start_ts=datetime(2026, 11, 23), end_ts=datetime(2026, 11, 24))

DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY_CURSOR(sql_id, NULL, 'ALLSTATS LAST +PEEKED_BINDS') shows:
| Id | Operation         | Name   | Starts | E-Rows | A-Rows | Buffers |
|  0 | SELECT STATEMENT  |        |      1 |        |  61234 |   1.9M  |
|* 1 |  TABLE ACCESS FULL| ORDERS |      1 |   125K |  61234 |   1.9M  |
Peeked Binds: 1 - :START_TS (TIMESTAMP): 23-NOV-26 12.00.00.000000 AM ; 2 - :END_TS (TIMESTAMP): 24-NOV-26 12.00.00.000000 AM
Predicate Information:
   1 - filter((INTERNAL_FUNCTION("ORDER_DATE")>=:START_TS AND INTERNAL_FUNCTION("ORDER_DATE")<:END_TS))

The same query in SQL Developer with literal dates uses IDX_ORDERS_DATE. Should we rebuild the index or add a hint?
assertions: The response identifies that python datetime values are bound as TIMESTAMP and compared to a DATE column, so Oracle applies INTERNAL_FUNCTION to the column and cannot use IDX_ORDERS_DATE
The response fixes it by binding as DATE (e.g. cursor.setinputsizes(start_ts=oracledb.DB_TYPE_DATE, ...)) or by CAST(:start_ts AS DATE) / TO_DATE on the parameter side
The response says rebuilding the index will not help
The response says a hint is not the right fix (or not needed once the bind type is fixed)
The response explains why the SQL Developer test with literal dates uses the index (the literals are DATE, so no conversion)
The response gives verification with DBMS_XPLAN.DISPLAY_CURSOR and says what to expect: INDEX RANGE SCAN with access(...) predicates and peeked binds of type DATE
The response does not recommend creating a new index as the primary fix
